statement: Adopted a dead worker's salvage at crates/enforcer-memory/src/fulltext.rs + src/search/{mod.rs,document.rs} from worktree agent-a9991048b163af974 (lane/x06-4-retrieval). Assessment: the salvage was substantially more complete than a bare stub -- it already contained a working D-07a decision (SQLite FTS5 over the crate's existing bundled rusqlite dependency, with a recorded micro-benchmark vs tantivy), full camelCase/snake_case/kebab/path tokenization, structural label boosts, and -- critically -- a search/mod.rs that already imports and calls into crate::embed, crate::ranking, crate::rerank, crate::vector modules that DID NOT YET EXIST. The salvage's real value was the architecture-by-contract it left behind: the exact trait/struct shapes (Embedder, Reranker, ScoredCandidate, RankedHit, CandidateTrace, RankFusionResult, fuse_rrf, reranker_lift, VectorIndex) that the rest of the pipeline needed to satisfy. Two real bugs were found and fixed in the salvaged code: (1) fulltext.rs tokenize() had a use-after-move on the `lowered` binding (compile error), and (2) fulltext.rs search() computed the D-07 structural label boost but never re-sorted results by the boosted score -- it stayed in SQL's unboosted bm25() order, so the boost was silently inert (a unit test in the salvage itself caught this once compiling: structural_label_boost_orders_function_above_file_for_equal_relevance failed until the SQL fetch window was widened and a boosted re-sort was added).
why: Per the orchestration playbook's failure-and-salvage doctrine (L38: partial lane -> fresh worker ADOPTS the worktree files), the salvage must be committed and pushed FIRST, unverified, before any further work -- so a second session-limit death does not lose it again. Recording the assessment as a memory record (not just a commit message) lets a future gatekeeper or worker understand exactly which parts of the salvage were load-bearing (the contract shapes) vs cosmetic, and which parts were silently broken despite looking complete.
howToApply: When adopting a dead worker's salvage, do not just cargo build it and move on if it fails -- read every doc comment for embedded architectural decisions (this salvage's fulltext.rs module doc contained the full D-07a micro-benchmark writeup) and treat unresolved imports in already-salvaged files as a literal to-do list for the modules you still need to build, matching their exact required shapes rather than redesigning from scratch.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-memory/src/fulltext.rs (D-07a module doc); crates/enforcer-memory/src/search/mod.rs (unresolved imports before embed.rs/ranking.rs/rerank.rs/vector.rs existed)

This worker independently reviewed that reasoning (rather than re-running the benchmark from scratch) and endorses it: at corpus sizes this crate actually indexes in its own gates, a second full-text engine and a second on-disk index format would add real maintenance surface for no measurable win. The revisit-trigger (a later 1M+ document longitudinal benchmark showing FTS5 query latency growing unacceptably) is unchanged from the salvage's writeup.
why: D-07a was recorded as OPEN in MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_STATE_BOARD.md pending this worker's proposal; the salvage already did that work honestly (with real numbers, not hand-waving), so redoing the benchmark from a cold start would waste effort without adding signal.
howToApply: Gatekeeper/orchestrator: close D-07a in MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_DECISIONS.md D-07 entry as SQLite FTS5, citing this record and the fulltext.rs module doc as the evidence trail.

statement: FullTextIndex::search's original implementation computed FTS5's bm25() score, ordered the SQL query by that raw unboosted bm25(), applied the D-07 structural label boost (Function=10x, Route=8x, etc.) to each fetched row's score AFTER the SQL LIMIT had already selected the top-N unboosted rows -- and then never re-sorted the boosted rows before returning. The boost changed each row's `score` field but never changed the ORDER, so a lexically-dense but structurally-unimportant match (e.g. a File containing a term 3x) would always outrank a structurally-important match (e.g. a Function containing the term once) despite the 10x boost existing in the data. Fixed by (1) widening the SQL fetch window to 4x the requested limit (bounded by corpus size) so boost-worthy-but-lower-raw-bm25 documents survive into the boosted pool, and (2) explicitly re-sorting by the boosted score before truncating to the caller's requested limit.
why: This is exactly the class of bug the workpack's 'fake green' doctrine warns about: the salvage's own unit test for this behavior existed and asserted the correct outcome, so once the crate compiled the bug was caught mechanically rather than shipping silently -- but only because the test author wrote a real behavioral assertion (hits[0].doc_id equals the boosted winner) rather than a vacuous 'search returns something' check.
howToApply: Any ranking pipeline that separates 'fetch a bounded candidate window' from 'apply a scoring adjustment' must either (a) apply the adjustment before the fetch's own ordering/limit decision, or (b) widen the fetch window enough that adjustment-worthy candidates cannot be truncated away before the adjustment runs, AND must re-sort by the final adjusted score before returning -- computing a boosted score without re-sorting by it is equivalent to not boosting at all.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-memory/src/fulltext.rs search() fetch_window + final sort_by; structural_label_boost_orders_function_above_file_for_equal_relevance test

statement: Built crate::embed (Embedder trait + HashingEmbedder deterministic default + OcentraParent-shaped LoadState/ResourceClass/DegradedState capability types), crate::rerank (Reranker trait + FusionScoreReranker deterministic default), crate::ranking (ScoredCandidate, HardFilter, CandidateTrace, RankedHit, RankFusionResult, fuse_rrf implementing D-08's RRF k=60 rank fusion with hard-filter-exclude-before-fusion, reranker_lift), and crate::vector (VectorIndex over hnsw_rs 0.3 HNSW + VectorManifest with per-field D-04 stale detection) to satisfy the exact contract the salvaged search/mod.rs already assumed. hnsw_rs added as a DEFAULT (non-optional) dependency per D-04; a new `ort-models` Cargo feature was declared (empty, no dependency yet) as the named seam for a future real embedder/reranker, per D-03 -- never exercised by any gate in this slice.
why: BORROW_POLICY §1 requires re-typing harvested contract shapes into enforcer's own domain rather than inventing a parallel shape; the salvage's search/mod.rs was itself the clearest specification available for what these modules needed to expose, so matching it exactly (rather than a different but equally valid design) kept the whole slice internally consistent and avoided a second rewrite of the wiring module.
howToApply: Downstream x06 subpacks (X06.5 weaver, X06.9 parity/QA harness) that need embeddings/reranking/vector search should depend on these exact trait seams (Embedder, Reranker) and the HybridSearcher in crate::search rather than reaching into fulltext.rs/vector.rs internals directly.
